newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks WTO to delay naming Helms-Burton panel.
newsitem.headline: EU asks WTO to delay naming Helms-Burton panel.

text.p: The European Union has asked World Trade Organisation chief Renato Ruggiero to delay naming a panel to rule on complaints that Washington's Helms-Burton Act contravenes world trade rules.

European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said in a statement released on Wednesday that he had asked Ruggeiro to delay naming the panel until February 20 in an attempt to reach a settlement with the U.S.
The EU and U.S. have been at odds for nearly a year over the act, an amalgamation of years of Washington's anti-Cuba policy.

Among other things, the act allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreign individuals or companies benefiting from investments in property confiscated by Havana since the communist revolution of 1959.
This part was suspended by U.S. president Bill Clinton in January, but the EU nevertheless proceeded with a complaint at the WTO.

Brittan said is was "not credible" for the U.S. to claim the WTO should not rule on the matter as it was a national security issue, but said he would be prepared to delay having a panel named in order for further discussions with Washington.
